title: The Burning Veil
premise: Freya Marchetti has guarded the sealed Ember Gate beneath the city of Vhalen for ten years, hiding her magic in a world that outlawed it after the Dragon Wars. When her new date, Elias Thorn, appears verbatim in a century-old prophecy, she realizes he is the Veilborn — a living key that can reopen the gate and free the last dragon, whose dying fire keeps the city's wards alive. As the Ashen Order hunts them both and Freya's own hidden heritage as half-veilblood surfaces, she must choose between loyalty to the order that raised her and the truth that the gate was never meant to imprison the dragon but to starve it. In the end, Freya opens the gate willingly, feeds the dragon her own veilblood to renew its fire, and shatters the prophecy itself — buying Vhalen a future no book has written.
about_author: W. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing banned grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about gatekeepers, outcasts, and the quiet cost of keeping secrets.

chapters.title: Charms for the Lawless
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She sells a luck charm to a nervous dockworker, then meets Elias for a first date at a night market. Warm, wry tone establishes her double life and loneliness; the beat is cautious hope.

chapters.title: The Book That Knew Him
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Back at the gatehouse, she consults the Prophecy Ledger for routine ward-checks and finds Elias's name, face, and tonight's words transcribed a century ago. The emotional beat is dread blooming under wonder.

chapters.title: Second Date, First Omen
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He notices Freya flinching at coincidences — his birthmark, a phrase he repeats. When an Ashen Order patrol sweeps the market, Freya pulls him into the tunnels. Beat: intimacy shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: Beneath the Ember Gate
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She shows Elias the sealed gate and confesses her role as keeper. The dragon's fire gutters visibly behind the stone. Beat: trust offered as a gamble.

chapters.title: The Order Knocks
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Warden Cassian Vey arrives demanding the Ledger; Freya hides Elias. Flashback reveals Cassian saved child-Freya after her mother's execution. Beat: loyalty tested by suspicion.

chapters.title: Veilborn
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Reading the prophecy aloud, he triggers a resonance — the gate hums, his veins glow faintly. He learns he was born the night the last dragon egg died. Beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: What the Wards Cost
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A ward fails in the Lower City; a child is hurt by leaking wild-magic. Freya heals her in secret, nearly caught. Beat: guilt — the system she serves is starving the city too.

chapters.title: Cassian's Bargain
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. He reveals he knows about Elias and offers protection in exchange for handing him over before the Solstice Rite. Flashbacks show Cassian's own buried magic. Beat: the antagonist as a mirror.

chapters.title: Running on Cobblestones
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Freya and Elias flee through Vhalen's rooftops and canal-tunnels, growing closer while dodging Order hunters. Beat: love kindling inside pursuit.

chapters.title: The Ash Archive
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. An exiled scholar, Maren, shows them the uncensored history: the gate was built to siphon the dragon's fire, not contain its rage. Beat: truth as betrayal of everything taught.

chapters.title: Half-Veilblood
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Maren identifies Freya's mother as a veilblood priestess — Freya can feed or drain the gate herself. Beat: the hunted discovers she is the weapon.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. The Order prepares to sacrifice Elias at the Rite to 'renew' the wards — actually to finish draining the dragon. Cassian hesitates. Beat: doubt in the hunter.

chapters.title: Captured
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya surrenders herself to save Elias from ambush; they are separated. Beat: sacrifice and helplessness.

chapters.title: The Gilded Cage
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Imprisoned in the Order spire, Elias is courted gently by High Warden Ilse, who claims the dragon must die for the city to live. Beat: persuasion versus instinct.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Cassian interrogates Freya; she turns it, forcing him to admit he's known the wards were failing for years. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made explicit between old allies.

chapters.title: Maren's Price
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The scholar trades the escape route for a promise: if the gate opens, the archives burn with her. Beat: complicity and grief.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Spire
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Freya and Elias reunite mid-escape; Freya's veilblood erupts, tearing the spire's wards apart. Beat: power embraced, innocence lost.

chapters.title: Dragonfire, Dying
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the gate, they meet the dragon Ysolde — ancient, lucid, nearly extinguished — who confirms the prophecy's trap: opening it unprepared reignites the war. Beat: awe and terrible choice.

chapters.title: Ilse's War
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. High Warden Ilse orders the gate destroyed outright, which will kill the dragon and blind the city to the true threat beyond the veil. Cassian defects. Beat: allegiance reversed.

chapters.title: The Last Rite
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Climax at the gate: Ilse's forces, the failing wards, and the thinning veil all converge. Freya chooses to pour her veilblood into Ysolde as Elias anchors the gate open. Beat: self-giving at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Ashes and Embers
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Ilse falls into the veil's hunger; Cassian holds the line; the dragon's fire rekindles and rewrites the wards honestly. Freya survives, changed — marked, diminished, free. Beat: victory with scars.

chapters.title: A Future Unwritten
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Weeks later: magic decriminalized slowly, the Ledger's final page blank, Freya and Elias reopening the night-market stall together. Beat: belonging found, identity chosen, story open-ended but whole.
